Measuring Talent Pipelines in Emerging Fields
Emerging fields face a recurring
problem: demand for skilled people
grows faster than the systems that
produce them. Universities
respond slowly, employers
compete for a small pool of
experienced candidates, and
newcomers struggle to find
credible entry points.
We studied three such fields over
a decade and found that short,
intensive programs filled a gap that
neither degrees nor on-the-job
training could. The most effective
combined a demanding application
process with substantial peer
interaction.
Our analysis suggests that the
binding constraint is rarely the
number of interested applicants. It
is the number of organisations able
to absorb and develop new talent
quickly, which in turn depends on
management capacity and funding
stability.
We conclude with several
proposals for funders, including
multi-year commitments to
absorptive organisations and
shared infrastructure for recruiting
and assessment across the field.
